First, we rewrite the denominator using $1-{cos}^{2}⁡x={sin}^{2}⁡x.$

$$
\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}{2{sin}^{2}⁡x}=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}{2(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)}
$$

Next, we factor the denominator as difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}{2(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}{2(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =-\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =-\frac{\cancel{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{2\cancel{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{1}{-2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=-2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).$
